title: P-F* causal direction is not identified by cross-sectional covariance

setup.observed_cross_sectional_pattern: P-associated regions and F*/EMT-associated changes co-occur in human AGA tissue

known_answer.model_1: F* -> P with coefficient 0.6 and residual variance 0.64
known_answer.model_2: P -> F* with coefficient 0.6 and residual variance 0.64

invariants: Observational Equivalence Can Hide Intervention Divergence
P-F* Direction Requires Perturbation, Temporal Ordering, or Stronger Causal Assumptions
HF01_consequence: GSE282856 strengthens the existence of a spatial P/F* association but does not authorize the claim that fibrosis/EMT causes progenitor loss. The next high-value experiment should perturb the candidate structural context and measure progenitor function plus later follicle output, or perturb progenitor state and test structural response.
boundary: The linear Gaussian SCM is a mathematical counterexample demonstrating non-identifiability. It is not a quantitative model of AGA biology.
